item.title: Yemen’s Health Ministry raises alarm over ‘near depletion’ of medical, fuel supplies in Taiz
item.description:
Yemen’s Health Ministry raises alarm over ‘near depletion’ of medical, fuel supplies in Taiz

Yemen’s Health Ministry warned on Sunday of “serious health and humanitarian repercussions” facing the city of Taiz as a result of the Houthis' obstruction of the delivery of essential supplies.

“The near depletion of medicines, medical solutions, supplies and fuel in health facilities threatens the cessation of several life-saving medical services,” a statement from the ministry was quoted by Saba news agency as saying, demanding “the immediate lifting of the siege, the opening of supply routes and the guarantee of safe passage for patients, ambulances, medical personnel and humanitarian aid to the city”.

item.title: Senior military commander says Iran will continue to strike vessels ‘if necessary’
item.description:
Senior military commander says Iran will continue to strike vessels ‘if necessary’

Iranian forces will continue to strike vessels in the Strait of Hormuz “if necessary”, senior Iranian military commander and deputy army coordinator Habibollah Sayyari said on Sunday. 

“We have dealt blows to enemy vessels, and if something happens against Iran again, we will strike at them. We are not tied, and we have facilities and capabilities that are specific and general in the world,” he said in comments carried by Iranian media.

item.title: Iraq, EU leaders denounce alleged Houthi attack on Riyadh airport
item.description:
Iraq, EU leaders denounce alleged Houthi attack on Riyadh airport

Several international leaders issued condemnations on Sunday following the alleged Houthi attack a day earlier on Saudi Arabia's King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. 

Iraq called for a "comprehensive cessation of military operations", adding that the attack endangered "regional security and stability" and threatened civilians, according to a statement from the prime minister's spokesman, Sabah al-Numan.

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said he "firmly condemns" what he described as "a terrorist act against Saudi Arabia and civil aviation", adding that "our thoughts are with the victims and I send my sincere condolences to their loved ones" in a post on X.

UK Defence Minister Wes Streeting also condemned the attack as a "dangerous escalation".

"This is completely contemptible action and it's one of the reasons why the UK is providing support to Saudi Arabia in the form of air defences, but also air-to-air refuelling," he told Sky News on Sunday.

EU chief Ursula von der Leyen called for the attacks on civilians to cease and said the European bloc stands in "solidarity with Saudi Arabia", accusing the Houthis, whom she referred to as "Iran's proxies", of "pushing the region into a spiral of violence" and destabilising global energy supplies.

item.title: Iran’s Gharibabadi says Minab school attackers must face justice
item.description:
Iran’s Gharibabadi says Minab school attackers must face justice

Iran’s Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi on Sunday called for the “aggressors” behind the attack on Minab school, which took place on the first day of the US-Israeli war on Iran, killing 156 people, including 120 children, to be held accountable through legal proceedings and in “international forums”.

“Excellent documentation of this crime has been collected and sent to Tehran, and an indictment has been issued. Some foreign countries have filed lawsuits regarding Minab’s crime,” he said, in comments carried by Iran’s IRIB broadcaster.

Gharibabadi added that the US had yet to accept responsibility for the attack, despite numerous reports and documents indicating US involvement.

item.title: After RAF Fairford incident, how big a threat to the UK is Iran?
item.description:
Although there is scepticism about Tehran’s capabilities, it has become clear it wants Britain to feel it poses a risk

Britain may have been only peripherally involved in the bombing of Iran that Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu started, but in the past fortnight it has become clear that Tehran wants to pose a threat inside the UK in response.

In the aftermath of the confused incident near RAF Fairford, western officials are weighing up whether to warn publicly that Iran now has US military targets in Europe on its mind, such as the air force base in Gloucestershire.
